stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that waited with four other people

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

columns.label: Mean score on the final test (%)

rows.group: The group that took practice quizzes
The group that reread the passage

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They hypothesized that the treatment would affect the severity of depression.

**Participants.** The sample was 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

**Results.** The group that received therapy: mean depression score = 11. The group on the waiting list: mean depression score = 21. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 90 students were randomly assigned to study 40 vocabulary words either in six ten-minute sessions on different days or in one sixty-minute session. One month later, the spaced group recalled a mean of 27 words and the single-session group a mean of 16 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** In an experiment, 120 students read a passage and were randomly assigned either to take three practice quizzes or to reread the passage three times. On a test one week later, the quiz group scored a mean of 68 percent and the rereading group 49 percent (p = 0.01).

**Source C.** In a survey of 600 students, 71 percent said that rereading notes was their main study method, and most rated it as highly effective. Only 12 percent said that they regularly tested themselves.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes regression?

options.text: The defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses
options.why: That describes reaction formation.

options.text: The defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness
options.why: That describes repression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities
options.why: That describes sublimation.

options.text: The defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development
options.why: Correct. This is what regression means.

questions.explanation: Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.

questions.stem: Although she dislikes the film, Ida says she loved it because all her friends did and she wants to fit in. Which kind of influence is this?

options.why: Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.
Correct. Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.
The peripheral route to persuasion is persuasion that works through surface cues, such as an attractive or famous speaker.
The central route to persuasion is persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully.

questions.explanation: Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.

questions.stem: A therapist keeps every appointment, honors his commitments and protects the trust his clients place in him. Which ethical principle is he following?

options.why: Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.
Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.
Correct. Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.

questions.explanation: Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

questions.stem: A shy teenager avoids parties, so she gets little social practice, which makes her even more shy. This interaction between thoughts, behavior and environment is called which of the following?

options.why: Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.
A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.
Correct. Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.
Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.

questions.explanation: Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere?

options.why: Correct. Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.
Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.
A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.
Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.

questions.explanation: Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.

questions.stem: Students at one school say, 'People at that other school are all the same,' while describing their own classmates as varied individuals. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.
Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.
In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.
Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.

questions.explanation: Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: With her eyes closed, Uma can still touch her nose with her fingertip. Which sense makes this possible?

options.why: The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
Correct. Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.

questions.explanation: Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes modeling?

options.text: The process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate
options.why: Correct. This is what modeling means.

options.text: Learning from seeing the consequences of another person's behavior
options.why: That describes vicarious conditioning.

options.text: A mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings
options.why: That describes a cognitive map.

options.text: Learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it
options.why: That describes latent learning.

questions.explanation: Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes groupthink?

options.text: The strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them
options.why: That describes group polarization.

options.text: The improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others
options.why: That describes social facilitation.

options.text: The reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present
options.why: That describes diffusion of responsibility.

options.text: The kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives
options.why: Correct. This is what groupthink means.

questions.explanation: Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.

questions.stem: An eight-year-old answers the questions that a typical ten-year-old can answer. On Binet's test, ten is the child's what?

options.why: The Flynn effect is the steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations.
Correct. Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.
Multiple intelligences is the theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal.
The intelligence quotient is originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100.

questions.explanation: Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The number of hours of social media use per day
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes discontinuous development?

options.text: Research that compares people of different ages at one point in time
options.why: That describes a cross-sectional study.

options.text: The developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person
options.why: That describes nature and nurture.

options.text: The view that development is a gradual, steady process, like a ramp
options.why: That describes continuous development.

options.text: The view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase
options.why: Correct. This is what discontinuous development means.

questions.explanation: Discontinuous development is the view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

options.text: Whether a small request came first
options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Which sense detects the basic qualities of sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus?

options.why: A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.
Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.
Correct. Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.

questions.explanation: Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.

questions.stem: A scan shows which brain areas receive more oxygen-rich blood while a volunteer solves puzzles. Which technique is this?

options.why: Correct. An fMRI is a scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow.
An EEG is a recording of the electrical waves that sweep across the brain's surface.
A case study is an in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage.
Lesioning is the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function.

questions.explanation: An fMRI is a scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: The night before a test, Gia studies for six hours without a break. Which kind of practice is she using?

options.why: Chunking is the organizing of items into familiar, manageable units.
Correct. Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.
The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.
A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.

questions.explanation: Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.

questions.stem: Kai is consistently attracted to people of the same sex. Which term describes this pattern of attraction?

options.why: Gender identity is a person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination.
A gender role is the set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women.
Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.
Correct. Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.

questions.explanation: Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.

questions.stem: A therapist does not give advice; she listens with empathy and accepts whatever her client says, trusting the client to find his own answers. Which therapy is this?

options.why: Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.
Active listening is the technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says.
Hypnosis is a state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories.
Correct. Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.

questions.explanation: Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times?

options.why: Dissociative amnesia is the disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue).
Correct. Dissociative identity disorder is the disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times.
Posttraumatic stress disorder is the disorder in which a person has flashbacks, nightmares, watchfulness and avoidance for more than a month after a terrifying event.
An obsession is an unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety.

questions.explanation: Dissociative identity disorder is the disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The amount of caffeine consumed each day
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A case study examines one individual in depth.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a specific learning disorder?

options.text: The eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise
options.why: That describes bulimia nervosa.

options.text: The neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence
options.why: Correct. This is what a specific learning disorder means.

options.text: The eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward
options.why: That describes binge-eating disorder.

options.text: The neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness
options.why: That describes attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.

questions.explanation: A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes experimenter bias?

options.text: The influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study
options.why: Correct. This is what experimenter bias means.

options.text: The tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments
options.why: That describes overconfidence.

options.text: The tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good
options.why: That describes social desirability bias.

options.text: The inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings
options.why: That describes self-report bias.

questions.explanation: Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.

questions.stem: Ben is tormented by constant worry and feels miserable most of the day. Which criterion for a psychological disorder does this meet?

options.why: Deviation from the social norm is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects.
Correct. Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.
The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.
Stigma is the negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder.

questions.explanation: Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.

questions.stem: Railway tracks in a drawing appear to come together at the horizon, which makes the scene look deep. Which depth cue is this?

options.why: Texture gradient is the monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away.
Convergence is the binocular depth cue based on how far the eyes turn inward to focus on a near object.
Retinal disparity is the binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes.
Correct. Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.

questions.explanation: Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.

questions.stem: Although he is not hungry, Karl buys a cake because it looks and smells delicious. Which theory of motivation best explains this?

options.why: The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.
Correct. Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.
Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.
Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.

questions.explanation: Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 9, 7, 3, 15, 5, 7, 10. What is the range of the scores?

options.why: That is the median.
That is the mean.
Correct. Subtract the lowest score from the highest.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 3, 5, 7, 7, 9, 10, 15. Subtract the lowest score from the highest. The one very high score pulls the mean (8) above the median (7), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings?

options.why: The macrosystem is in ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child.
Correct. The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.
The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.
The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.

questions.explanation: The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: Each night, Noor writes down three things she is thankful for, and over time she feels happier. Which practice is this?

options.why: Correct. Gratitude is the appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being.
Resilience is the ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship.
Signature strengths is the positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person.
Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.

questions.explanation: Gratitude is the appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being.

questions.stem: A psychologist says rates of eating disorders are higher where the culture promotes an extremely thin body ideal. Which perspective is this?

options.why: Correct. The sociocultural perspective is the view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination.
The psychodynamic perspective is the view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood.
The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.
The behavioral perspective is the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement.

questions.explanation: The sociocultural perspective is the view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes state-dependent memory?

options.text: The improved recall that occurs in the same physical state as when the information was learned
options.why: Correct. This is what state-dependent memory means.

options.text: The identification of previously learned information when it is presented, as in a multiple-choice question
options.why: That describes recognition.

options.text: The finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading
options.why: That describes the testing effect.

options.text: The tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood
options.why: That describes mood-congruent memory.

questions.explanation: State-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same physical state as when the information was learned.

questions.stem: A grid of letters is flashed for an instant, and viewers can still 'see' it for a moment afterward. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Correct. Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.
Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.
Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.
Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.

questions.explanation: Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced?

options.why: Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.
A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.
A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.
Correct. A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.

questions.explanation: A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for fight or flight?

options.why: Correct. The sympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for fight or flight.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.
The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.
The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.

questions.explanation: The sympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for fight or flight.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options?

options.why: An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.
Correct. An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.
Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.

questions.explanation: An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: Conscientiousness score on a personality inventory
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The number of hours worked in a paid job
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes displacement?

options.text: The defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality
options.why: That describes denial.

options.text: The defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior
options.why: That describes rationalization.

options.text: The defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one
options.why: Correct. This is what displacement means.

options.text: The defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people
options.why: That describes projection.

questions.explanation: Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.stem: Although the film is terrible, Mo stays to the end because he already paid for the ticket. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.
The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.
The availability heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind.
Framing is the way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments.

questions.explanation: The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see?

options.why: Correct. Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.
Gross motor skills is the movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping.
Fine motor skills is the movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt.
A critical period is a limited time early in life when certain experiences must occur for normal development.

questions.explanation: Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.

questions.stem: In the strange situation, a toddler shows little reaction when her mother leaves and turns away when she returns. Which attachment style is this?

options.why: Correct. Avoidant attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return.
Anxious attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child is very upset by separation and is not easily comforted on reunion.
Contact comfort is the comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding.
Separation anxiety is the distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months.

questions.explanation: Avoidant attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return.

questions.stem: Witnesses asked how fast the cars were going when they 'smashed' into each other later remember broken glass that was not there. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.
Correct. The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.
Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.
Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.

questions.explanation: The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.

questions.stem: Grandpa tells detailed stories about his wedding day and his first job. Which kind of memory is he drawing on?

options.why: Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.
Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Correct. Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.

questions.explanation: Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior?

options.why: Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.
Correct. The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.
A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.

questions.explanation: The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness?

options.why: The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.
Proactive interference is the disruption of new learning by older memories.
Correct. Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.
Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.

questions.explanation: Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.

questions.stem: After a message has been sent, the sending neuron takes back the neurotransmitter molecules that remain in the gap. What is this process called?

options.why: The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.
The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.
Correct. Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.
The action potential is the brief electrical charge that travels down the axon when a neuron fires.

questions.explanation: Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.

questions.stem: After effective drugs were introduced, large numbers of patients were released from psychiatric hospitals to live in the community. What is this change called?

options.why: Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.
Correct. Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.
The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.
Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.

questions.explanation: Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain?

options.why: The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.
The cerebral cortex is the wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement.
Correct. The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.

questions.explanation: The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.

questions.stem: For months, Hana has lain awake for hours each night and woken long before her alarm. Which sleep disorder does she most likely have?

options.why: REM sleep behavior disorder is a sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams.
Correct. Insomnia is a sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.
Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.

questions.explanation: Insomnia is a sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions?

options.why: Correct. An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.
Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.
A situational attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances.
The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.

questions.explanation: An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.

questions.stem: A client with borderline personality disorder learns mindfulness, ways of tolerating distress and ways of regulating emotions. Which therapy is this?

options.why: The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.
Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.
Correct. Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.
Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.

questions.explanation: Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes integrity versus despair?

options.text: Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are
options.why: That describes identity versus role confusion.

options.text: Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work
options.why: That describes generativity versus stagnation.

options.text: Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret
options.why: Correct. This is what integrity versus despair means.

options.text: Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships
options.why: That describes intimacy versus isolation.

questions.explanation: Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.
Debriefing happens after the study.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an operational definition?

options.text: A statement of exactly how a variable is measured or manipulated in a study
options.why: Correct. This is what an operational definition means.

options.text: The research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect
options.why: That describes an experiment.

options.text: The research method of watching and recording behavior in its natural setting without interfering
options.why: That describes naturalistic observation.

options.text: The research method that measures two variables to see how they are related, without manipulating either
options.why: That describes a correlational study.

questions.explanation: An operational definition is a statement of exactly how a variable is measured or manipulated in a study.

questions.stem: During a near-miss in traffic, glands above the kidneys release a hormone that makes the driver's heart race. Which hormone is this?

options.why: Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.
Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.
Correct. Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Melatonin is the hormone released by the pineal gland that makes a person sleepy.

questions.explanation: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.

questions.stem: A dog's salivation to a tone has died away. The next day, the tone is sounded and the dog salivates again. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.
Acquisition is in classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned.
Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.
Correct. Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.

questions.explanation: Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.

questions.stem: A stroke in the left motor cortex paralyzes a patient's right arm. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.
Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.
Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.
Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.

questions.explanation: Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a reuptake inhibitor?

options.text: A drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it
options.why: That describes an agonist.

options.text: The unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug
options.why: That describes withdrawal.

options.text: A drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption
options.why: Correct. This is what a reuptake inhibitor means.

options.text: A drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors
options.why: That describes an antagonist.

questions.explanation: A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.

questions.stem: Before a study begins, each adult volunteer reads a description of the procedures and risks and signs a form agreeing to take part. Which ethical requirement is this?

options.why: An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.
Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.
Protection from harm is the requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible.
Correct. Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.

questions.explanation: Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate?

options.why: Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.
Correct. Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.

questions.explanation: Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.

questions.stem: Over several years, a young man slowly becomes more withdrawn and odd, and his symptoms persist for decades. Which pattern is this?

options.why: An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
Correct. A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.
The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.
A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.

questions.explanation: A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation?

options.why: Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.
Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
Correct. A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.
Taijin kyofusho is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly in Japan, marked by fear of offending or embarrassing others.

questions.explanation: A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike?

options.why: Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.
Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.
Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.
Correct. Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.

questions.explanation: Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.

options.text: The behavior of an adult model
options.why: This is the independent variable.

options.text: The number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = +0.75. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship with the negative sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: After many years on antipsychotic medication, a patient develops uncontrollable movements of the mouth and tongue. Which side effect is this?

options.why: Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.
Correct. Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.
An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.

questions.explanation: Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.

questions.stem: At seventy, Mr. Park does better at crossword puzzles and vocabulary tests than he did at thirty. Which kind of intelligence does this show?

options.why: Scaffolding is the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes.
The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.
Correct. Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.
Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.

questions.explanation: Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.

questions.stem: After an infection damaged the tiny bones of his middle ear, Arun's hearing was restored with a hearing aid that amplifies sound. Which kind of hearing loss did he have?

options.why: Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.
Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.
Correct. Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.
Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.

questions.explanation: Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression?

options.why: A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.
Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.
Correct. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.
Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.

questions.explanation: Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of the severity of depression

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of the severity of depression.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: The severity of depression was defined as each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The therapy group had lower depression scores. On average, the value was 11 for the group that received therapy and 21 for the group on the waiting list, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The therapy group had lower depression scores. (11 compared with 21).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the treatment affects the severity of depression. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the treatment. The finding illustrates cognitive-behavioral therapy, which reduces depression by changing negative thought patterns (the cognitive triad) and behavior.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Spacing study sessions and testing oneself lead to better long-term learning than cramming or rereading.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who spread their study over six days recalled 27 of 40 words a month later, compared with 16 for students who studied in one session.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the spacing effect: distributed practice gives repeated chances to encode and consolidate the material, so it is retained longer than with massed practice.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who took practice quizzes scored 68 percent a week later, compared with 49 percent for students who reread the passage.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the testing effect: retrieving information from memory strengthens the memory and its retrieval cues more than rereading does.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
